4.0.s.en: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

4.0.0.en: The Lord spoke: an expression common throughout the book, meaning that God is the source of the command and direction. The command here is to number the sons of Kohath with all their clans. It is known that Kohath was the second son of Levi and not the firstborn, but the Kohathites come first here because of the greatness of the tasks with which they will be charged, which include the inner implements of worship, as we shall see (v. 4).

4.1.0.en: This numbering is new. After God charged Moses to number all the males from a month old, to be taken as a ransom for the firstborn of all the people (ch. 3), He asks him here for a new numbering, of the males from thirty years old to fifty, which is the age period in which a man is able to exert himself in work and to endure hardships.

4.1.1.en: Although the eighth chapter of this book (ch. 8:24) states that the age of enlistment for the service of the house of the Lord among the Levites is 25 years, the meaning is that from the age of 25 to 30 years is a period of training and of sharing in the lesser services. It is noted that in the days of David and Ezra (1 Chr 23:24-32; Ezra 3:8) enlistment was at the age of twenty, that is, there was a training period of ten years until they reached the age of thirty. John the Baptist and also Christ began their ministries at the age of thirty.

4.1.2.en: Although enlistment for war in the other tribes begins at the age of twenty (ch. 1:3), we find that enlistment for the service of the house of the Lord in the tribe of Levi begins at the age of thirty, because of the greatness and importance of the service of the house of the Lord above any other work.

4.1.3.en: All that enter into the host: God regarded what He would charge them with as exactly like enlistment, for the work in the tent of meeting is an awesome task that requires devotion and concentration. Indeed, the service of God in general requires the spirit of the fighting soldier, as St. Paul enjoined his disciple Timothy when he said to him, "Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ" (2 Tim 2:3).

4.1.4.en: My beloved brother, God in His love has called us to the service of His holy name, and because of the greatness of this calling He warns us to be soldiers in His service, watchful on guard. He does not accept the negligent or the slack, but curses him. So if you are a servant in the Church of God, be strong, look to the reward, and be watchful lest anyone take your crown.

4.2.0.en: God assigned the service of the Kohathites to the Holy of Holies, which is similar in its holiness to the sanctuary and the altar in the Church. It is the place where God was manifested when He appeared in His glory, and the ark of the covenant was placed in it. In fact, the service of the Kohathites included two places, "the sanctuary" and "the Holy of Holies," and everything they contain.

4.3.0.en: When the camp is to set forward: that is, when the divine command to depart or move was issued, and this command came by the pillar of cloud being lifted up from above the Tabernacle (Ex 40:36). When preparing to depart, Aaron and his sons, who are the priests and the only ones permitted to touch the holy things and the implements with their hands, began by taking down the veil that separated the sanctuary from the Holy of Holies, and covered the ark of the covenant with it.

4.4.0.en: As a second covering over the veil in which the ark was wrapped, they put the skin of a thick sea animal (badger), and then they bring a final outer covering, a cloth of sky-blue. It is noted that the ark and the table alone were covered with three coverings, while the rest of the implements would be covered with only two. "And shall put in the staves thereof": the staves by which the ark was carried were always kept in the side rings. This expression means that the covering also includes the staves, so that the Levites would not carry them with bare hands.

4.5.0.en: The table of showbread: the table placed in the sanctuary, on which twelve loaves are placed, representing the constant presence of the tribes before the face of God.

4.5.2.en: The way of covering the table before carrying it was as follows: first a cloth of blue ("hyacinth") is spread directly on the table, and over it is placed the bread, which must always be present before God, even when departing and journeying. The same applies to the implements used around the table, of dishes, bowls and cups.

4.6.0.en: The second covering comes over it, a cloth of scarlet, that is, red, the color of blood, and then the third covering over all of that, the thick skin that insulates, providing the highest degree of protection for the holy things by isolating them completely from dust. Symbolically, one may meditate on these coverings as follows ... The first, the sky-blue, points to Christ who comes from heaven to become incarnate, and who covered the twelve Apostles (the bread) with His glory. After that came the covering of the shed blood, which gives forgiveness and salvation, while the covering of thick skin points to the life of strictness in which the believer must live and by which he separates himself from evil.

4.6.1.en: And they put the staves in the rings of the table, which protrude outside the coverings, so that they may carry it by them. The Holy Bible says "the staves thereof," and it means the staves of the table of the showbread that was on the table.

4.7.0.en: The bar: two rods on which cross pieces of wood are fixed, to carry on it the lampstand or the other implements of the Tent.

4.7.1.en: As for the lampstand with seven lamps, whose place was in the sanctuary, it was covered with all its accessories and implements, the tongs and the oil vessels, first with a sky-blue covering and after that with an outer covering of the thick badger skin.

4.8.0.en: The golden altar: the inner altar of incense.

4.8.1.en: It too is covered with a blue cloth and then a covering of the skin of the thick badger animal.

4.9.0.en: As for the rest of the implements of the service that were not mentioned, such as the priests' garments or any other belongings, they are placed in the sky-blue cloth and also covered with the thick skin like the foregoing, and after this they are put on the carrier (the bar).

4.10.0.en: As for the outer altar of burnt offering, which is the bronze altar and whose place is at the entrance of the Tent, before covering it they had to remove the ashes left from the previous sacrifices and throw them in a place called "the place of the ashes," while the holy fire of the altar was carried in a special vessel throughout their journey. After the ashes and the holy fire were removed, they covered it with all its vessels needed for the service with a cloth of purple (royal red), since this altar, the altar of burnt offering, is a type of Christ the crucified King. Then comes after this the insulating covering of badger skin, and after covering the bronze altar they put its two staves in the rings and carried it by these staves.

4.10.1.en: The implements of the altar that are mentioned were:

4.10.2.en: The censers: the vessels in which burning coals are carried and which are used in burning incense, like the censer. The fleshhooks: a fork with three teeth and a long handle, used to take up or arrange the pieces of meat on the altar.

4.10.3.en: The shovels: the scoop used to shovel the ashes or to redistribute them on the altar.

4.10.4.en: The basins: vessels like bowls, used to collect the blood of the sacrifices so as to sprinkle it or throw it again as the matters of worship require.

4.11.0.en: The setting forward of the camp: the setting forward of the congregation of the children of Israel.

4.11.1.en: After the role of the priests, that is, Aaron and his sons, in wrapping and covering everything that was in the sanctuary and the Holy of Holies is finished, the role of the Levites comes, among them the sons of Kohath, and they carry these things without touching with their hands anything under these coverings, otherwise they would die. This is a strong warning from God to them, which makes them exceedingly careful in carrying and moving, and keeps far from them any suspicion of making light of these holy things.

4.12.0.en: Eleazar the son of Aaron had been appointed before this as general overseer of all the clans of the Levites in their work when setting forward or encamping (ch. 3:32), but here He makes clear other matters that were to be under his direct charge, which are:

4.12.1.en: - The oil for the light: the oil used to light the lamps of the lampstand.

4.12.2.en: - The sweet incense: the incense offered daily, morning and evening, on the altar of incense. - The daily meat offering: which is also the daily offering morning and evening (see Exodus 30:22-32). - The oversight of all the tabernacle: that is, no responsibility is excepted from Eleazar the priest, for everything is done under his personal and direct supervision.

4.13.0.en: God begins a new discourse with Moses and Aaron, laying on them a new responsibility, which is that the clans of the Kohathites not be cut off from the tribe of the Levites.

4.13.1.en: The meaning is that Aaron and his sons the priests must continually supervise, caution and warn the Kohathites, lest they touch any of the vessels or holy things with their hands and die and be cut off, and the negligence of Aaron and his sons the priests would be the cause of that, that is, the indirect cause of the destruction of the Kohathites.

4.13.2.en: How grave is the responsibility of the priests, since God has set them in the place of shepherds over His sheep, and He charges them with care and shepherding lest any of His flock perish, and Christ will require the blood of the sheep at the hand of the priest. If the responsibility is so great and fearful ... then, my brother, will you accept teaching or warning or even rebuke, if God allows it from the mouth of the priest ... If only you would do so, then you will not be cut off nor perish from before the Lord.

4.14.0.en: This warning came as a confirmation and completion of what was said before: no clan of the clans of the Levites is allowed to enter the sanctuary or the Holy of Holies lest they die, for no one enters these two places except the priests alone, and the punishment is plain and explicit if anything contrary to this happens.

4.15.0.en: These three verses correspond exactly to verses (1-3) at the beginning of the chapter. As He said at the choosing of the Kohathites, He says here at the choosing of the Gershonites, as an introduction to the service that will be assigned to them.

4.16.0.en: The service and the burden: the service means the care of the things, while the burden is a reference to carrying them during moving and journeying. The service of the Gershonites can be set out in detail as follows:-

4.16.1.en: 1- The curtains of the tabernacle: that is, the coverings of the Tent from above and from the sides. They were made of the finest linen fabrics, and their colors were blue, purple and scarlet, a reference to the blue sky, the garments of the King, and the blood of the Redeemer.

4.16.2.en: 2- The tent of the congregation: that is, the outer coverings made of goats' hair.

4.16.3.en: 3- The outer covering: which was made of the skin of the sea animal, the badger.

4.16.4.en: 4- The hanging for the door of the tent of the congregation: the door on the east side, which was also of fine cloth.

4.17.0.en: After the previous verse spoke about carrying the inner things, this verse moves us to speak about carrying the parts of the outer court that surrounds the tent of meeting.

4.17.1.en: 1- The hangings of the court: those made of linen, five cubits high (see Ex 26:9-10).

4.17.2.en: 2- The hanging for the gate of the court: the outer door of the outer court, also on the east side, and its height is like the height of the hangings, that is, five cubits, and its breadth 20 cubits (Ex 27:16). The hangings of the outer court were like the wall that surrounds the Tent and the altar of burnt offering.

4.17.3.en: 3- The cords: the ropes that tied the various coverings of the Tent at departure, and any ropes used inside the Tent.

4.17.4.en: 4- All the instruments of their service: that is, all the other tools connected with the inner curtains or the outer coverings, and anything the service needs or that may be damaged, which no one makes except the Gershonites.

4.18.0.en: All the work of the Gershonites is done under the supervision of the high priest Aaron and his sons the priests as well, and they are entrusted with watchfulness and care, that is, guarding everything God entrusted to them, and their direct chief in the supervision is the priest Ithamar the son of Aaron.

4.18.1.en: Covering precious things preserves them ... If only you would not speak much without need, and would keep the word of God within you and think on it so as to apply it in your life, and would persuade people of the truth more than much speaking that has no effect.

4.19.0.en: As came by way of an introduction to the service of the previous groups.

4.20.0.en: The service of the Merarites was the heavy things, such as:

4.20.1.en: 1- The boards of the tabernacle (Ex 26:15-25:), which are the wooden boards overlaid with plates of gold and are regarded as the walls of the Tent.

4.20.2.en: 2- The bars of the tabernacle: wood also overlaid with gold, which binds the boards to one another by means of rings of gold (Ex 26:26-29).

4.20.3.en: 3- Its pillars and its sockets: that is, the pillars on which the veil and the hangings are hung, that is, the inner curtains that serve as doors for the sanctuary, the Holy of Holies and the outer door of the Tent; and the sockets are the silver bases on which the pillars are fixed (Ex 26:31, 32, 36, 37).

4.21.0.en: The discourse here is about the outer court and its furnishings:

4.21.1.en: 1- The pillars of the court round about: that is, the outer wooden pillars, and this also includes the silver rods that bind the pillars to one another.

4.21.2.en: 2- Their sockets: the bases on which the pillars of the enclosure stand, but here they are of bronze and not silver.

4.21.3.en: 3- The pins: which are of bronze and were around the outer court.

4.21.4.en: 4- The cords: the ropes belonging to the outer court, for tying them to the outer bronze pins to hold them fast.

4.21.5.en: 5- Their instruments and all their service: that is, all the equipment, contents, appurtenances and accessories. God commanded that lists be prepared defining the responsibility of each Levite in what he carries: "by name ye shall reckon the instruments," as a charge that he receives and hands over and watches over throughout the period of carrying so that nothing of it is lost.

4.21.6.en: My beloved brother, notice with me God's care for the implements of the service and how He regards them as a personal charge for which the Levite is held accountable ... How much more, then, is the charge of the souls entrusted to the bishop, the priest or the servant, which is far more precious, since their loss cannot be made good ... Have mercy on us, O Lord, and help us to serve all the souls in need, and complete the weakness of the work of Your servants ... Amen.

4.22.0.en: Likewise the priest Ithamar is responsible for them and supervises them, as he is also chief over the Gershonites.

5.0.s.en: (1) The separation of persons and the unclean

5.0.0.en: Leper: leprosy is a skin disease that people have differed in describing. It is either a disease resembling the skin disease psoriasis, which appears in the form of scaly patches on the skin ... or it may resemble the skin disease vitiligo, in which the color of the skin turns snow white, or it may be a skin disease that affects the nerves and causes pain ... Some see that the "leprosy" mentioned in the Old Testament was a general name embracing all the foregoing skin diseases and perhaps others as well. The word leprosy means in Hebrew (calamity), to indicate the severity and gravity of this disease, especially in its spiritual meaning, as we shall see. An issue: the discourse on issues of their various kinds came in the Book of Leviticus, such as the bodily discharges of a man and a woman, in which the person, the clothes and the bed are considered in a state of uncleanness requiring cleansing, if the matter was occasional, like a nocturnal emission or the monthly period; but if the matter was chronic or continuous, then the separation is outside the camp, which is the place where the people dwell (see Lev 15). Defiled by the dead: that is, everyone who touched a dead person or entered a tent in which there was a dead person ... The discourse about that came in the Book of Leviticus in many places, and it will also be mentioned in the Book of Numbers in the two chapters (12, 19). The speech of God to Moses was decisive, that he should separate every leper, or one with a continuing issue, or one defiled by the dead, to make clear an important meaning for the people ... for the holy God, who dwells in the midst of His people, never accepts sin in His presence, and because leprosy, the issue and death are either divine strokes resulting from sin, like leprosy in particular, or a sickness arising from sin, like the issue, and death is the wages of sin ... all these souls are separated in tents of their own outside the camp, for there is no fellowship of light with darkness. We note in this the following:

5.0.1.en: 1- In God's mercies they were not left in the wilderness to die, but were separated in a place of their own for the sake of repentance. So also the Church may separate (excommunicate) some of her children from Communion or from attending church because of their corruption and their refusal to repent, but she does not cast them away; rather she cares for them outside until they return healthy, as she separated the sinner of Corinth and then received him after his repentance (1 Cor 5:1-5; 2 Cor 2:5-11).

5.0.2.en: 2- The idea of separation also has two other purposes: preventing the spread of infection (the stumbling block) among the members of the camp (the Church), and likewise the decisive punishment is a deterrent to a person when he sees with his own eyes the result of sin, so that he avoids it.

5.0.3.en: Thus the Church has always been decisive in separating those who cause stumbling and in excommunicating heretics. The heretic who brings teachings foreign to the faith is more deadly and dangerous to the flock than the leper or the one with an issue, for he pollutes minds with his thoughts and ruins the faith of the Church which she received through time from her Christ and His pure Apostles ... So, beloved, let no pity take you for one who ruins souls, and remember the saying and warning of the Apostle, "Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person."

5.1.0.en: The punishment does not distinguish between man and woman, for sin is one for all, and there is no partiality or sparing of one sex over the other ... Everyone who sins or whom God smites with sickness as a result of sin is separated outside the congregation until he is cleansed, whether by the laws of purification that will come later, for one who touched a dead person or had an issue, where he was separated for a limited time, or by complete healing for one smitten with the disease of leprosy. God makes clear that the reason for their banishment is His concern that sin not be passed on to all: "that they defile not their camps." God used the expression "ye shall put out ... shall ye put out" twice in one sentence to stress the separation and not to be lax in it.

5.1.1.en: My beloved brother ... if God lives and dwells in you, then do not accept sin or the thought of it, and separate yourself from evil and the wicked so that you may save your life and not be affected by associating with them, for there is no one among us who is not affected by the atmosphere around him ... And draw nearer still to spiritual friends, so that you live in purity and cleanness.

5.2.0.en: The people obeyed all that God commanded Moses, with submission and with conviction of the duty of separating evil.

5.3.0.en: The discourse moved from the separation of the defiled to another matter, which is a man's treachery against his fellow man, and this discourse comes as a completion of what is found in the Book of Leviticus (ch. 6:1-7). We note in this verse the following:

5.3.1.en: 1- There is no difference between man and woman in committing any sin, for God regards everyone who sins as guilty, whatever his sex or color.

5.3.2.en: 2- To commit a trespass against the Lord: that is, even if the sin is directed from one person to another or against him, the wrong is in the first place directed at God Himself and at His person directly. For this reason David the prophet says, though he had sinned by adultery against the woman with whom he committed adultery, her and her husband, "Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight" (Ps 50).

5.3.3.en: 3- That soul be guilty: even if no one saw her, she is guilty and deserving of divine punishment, or of offering repentance to God and also to the one against whom she sinned.

5.4.0.en: After God defined the wrong of the soul that committed treachery or theft, He explains to us here the steps of repentance and remedy as follows:

5.4.1.en: 1- They shall confess their sin: that is, they offer repentance and confession first to God, and to the priest who will receive the sacrifice (v. 8), and to the one against whom they sinned. This confession, which proceeds in three directions, is beneficial for the human soul to make, because it is a harsh exposure of it, and perhaps God wanted by this to alert man to what sin will bring upon him, so that he is deterred and does not venture upon it.

5.4.2.en: This takes place now in the Church in the sacrament of confession, in which the penitent receives forgiveness of his sins, in addition to his peace of mind and the guidance he receives from the father of confession to help him not to fall.

5.4.3.en: 2- He shall recompense his trespass: God is just in His judgments ... it is unreasonable for a person to take something from his brother ... and say I am sorry ... rather he must return what he stole ... And we err if we think that sin is forgiven in the sacrament of confession without the person returning what he took from his brother, for God is very clear in His words: there is no forgiveness unless you return what you took.

5.4.4.en: 3- And add unto it the fifth part thereof: that is, an additional fifth on what you took or seized. This is considered a punishment for the one who took, so that a person is deterred and does not venture upon the wrong in the first place, and on the other hand it is considered compensation for the one whose right was taken, whether compensation for a material loss or for the feelings of distress that befell him when he learned of his loss or of what was taken from him, as Zacchaeus did for those from whom he had extorted their money (Lk 19:8).

5.5.0.en: But if the person wronged has died and has no heir or kinsman to whom the wrongdoer may return what he took, God does not acquit the wrongdoer of his guilt except by his returning what he took. In this case, however, the restitution is made to the Lord, who is represented here by the priest responsible for applying the laws of God ... And if by this action the right returns to its owner who was wronged, or to God, there remains something else, which is to complete the apology to God Himself by offering a ram, that is, a lamb, as a sacrifice of atonement for sin, a clear indication that the blood of the sacrifice, which signifies the blood of Christ, is alone what atones for and forgives the sins of man, as the Apostle says, "without shedding of blood is no remission" (Heb 9:22).

5.5.1.en: Be faithful in your dealings with others, so that God is pleased with you and blesses you, in addition to winning the love of those around you, so that you live in peace and tranquility. This is more important than any material gains you obtain by illegitimate means or seize from others.

5.6.0.en: Every offering: that is, the shoulder of the heave offering (the sacrifice), which was the right of the priest who performs the service (Ex 29:26-28). Of the holy things of the children of Israel: these are the vows and sacrifices offered by the people to the Lord.

5.6.1.en: Every man's hallowed things shall be his: that is, what a person offers to God, of prescribed sacrifices or vows, shall be for the priest.

5.6.2.en: In these two verses God speaks about the rights of the priests, for they are His children and His own, whom He commends to the people. And so that the people's honoring of the priest would not be a favor from them to him, God set it in the form of a law binding on the people. Everything that is offered to God, apart from the burnt offering, whether at the level of the people at the feasts or at the level of the individual as in vows, belongs to the priests' portion, as do the parts that God appointed for the priest from the peace offerings. The discourse here brings out for us the following meanings:

5.6.3.en: 1- God's concern for the priests, as we pointed out.

5.6.4.en: 2- Urging the people to honor them.

5.6.5.en: 3- Honoring them is honoring God Himself: "He that receiveth you receiveth me" (Mt 10:40).

5.6.6.en: The priesthood in the Church of the New Testament has acquired a higher and more exalted station, since the sacrifice has become living and eternal and is no longer the blood of goats and bulls ... Likewise the responsibility of the priest has become wider in teaching, administering, guiding and shepherding. Therefore we must all pray for our fathers the priests, that God may help them in their responsibility before Him, which is the salvation of their souls and the souls of all their blessed people.

5.7.s.en: (4) The law of jealousy and suspicion

5.7.0.en: The speech was from God to Moses, and He commanded him to tell his people the following provisions of the Law, relating to the woman who has departed from the way of truth and the law of marriage, "gone aside," and fallen into marital unfaithfulness, that is, adultery.

5.7.1.en: God's concern to expose the sin of the adulterous woman is useful for the following:

5.7.2.en: 1- Establishing peace and trust between the spouses so that the family lives in tranquility.

5.7.3.en: 2- The importance of purity and chastity for the married.

5.7.4.en: 3- This law declares that God knows all hidden things, and so it makes a person keep away from every sin even if no one sees him.

5.7.5.en: 4- Showing the right of the innocent, so that she is not wearied by false accusations.

5.8.0.en: Lie with seed: that is, complete adultery, or adultery that resulted in pregnancy.

5.8.1.en: Kept close: that is, she was able to hide her deed and her sin from people.

5.8.2.en: Taken: not caught in the sin.

5.8.3.en: The spirit of jealousy: a spirit of suspicion and anger.

5.8.4.en: God goes into the detailed description of the case should it occur, and says that if a woman committed complete adultery that resulted in pregnancy, and even if she was able to hide everything from people, but her husband was seized by jealousy and suspicion, whether his suspicion was well founded and his jealousy true, or the woman was innocent of what her husband accused her of and did nothing of the foregoing, then in order to be sure of his course of action he does what will be mentioned in the following verses:

5.9.0.en: The tenth part of an ephah: the ephah is a measure of grain, and its tenth is 2.3 liters.

5.9.1.en: The man brings his wife to the tent of meeting and meets the priest, and takes with him an offering of barley meal, which is cheap and available to all. Because this offering relates to sin, suspicion and unfaithfulness, and is not like the other offerings, God forbade adding to it the oil and frankincense usually added, because oil is a symbol of the Holy Spirit and His gladdening work, and frankincense (incense) points to pure prayers, and this does not apply at all to what is before us.

5.10.0.en: The priest takes the woman who is suspected and makes her stand at the door of the tent of meeting "before the Lord," and takes holy water from the water of the laver, as most interpreters think, though there are other opinions that it is living running water, or water taken from the law of the red heifer (ch. 19). He puts this water in one of the earthen vessels of the service that were in the Tent, and takes a little of the dust, which points to the shameful position in which this woman stands, and the dust also points to being broken down before God, as Abraham said when he began his speech with God, "I am but dust and ashes" (Gen 18:27). The aim of this rite is to encourage the sinning wife to repent.

5.11.0.en: Uncover the woman's head: he removes her head covering as a sign of her being accused and her innocence not yet being proved.

5.11.1.en: The bitter water that causeth the curse: it is the same holy water, and it was called the water of the curse because it brings the curse on the woman if she has sinned, and it was called bitter as a reference to the bitterness of sin and its consequences. It is said that the priest used to add to it a bitter plant or a very bitter substance such as myrrh or wormwood.

5.11.2.en: Under thy husband: that is, married and joined to your husband, and then you went aside from him.

5.11.3.en: The priest brings the accused woman and reminds her that she stands before the Lord, holding in her hands the offering of ground barley after her head has been uncovered, while the water of the curse is in the priest's hand. The priest begins to question her with a clear and direct question after she swears that she will tell the truth, and he makes clear to her that if she did not commit the sin or become defiled by it with another man, God will declare her innocence and the bitter water of the curse will do her no harm.

5.12.0.en: The priest continues his speech with the woman, telling her that if she has fallen into sin and wronged her husband and committed adultery with another man than her husband.

5.13.0.en: The priest charges the woman with an oath of cursing: he declares that the curse must come upon her.

5.13.1.en: A curse among thy people: that is, you will become an example among women and a byword that they speak about you.

5.13.2.en: The priest invokes the curse on the woman. The curse will not come upon her unless she is guilty, and he says to her that you will be a curse instead of a blessing and become a mockery among your people. As for her bodily punishment, it is the sagging of her belly together with its visible swelling, and likewise her thigh, which was defiled by sin, will be afflicted with slackness and inability to walk (like paralysis ...). All this will be because of the water that she is now going to drink, which brings these curses upon her, and the woman answers affirming, "Amen, amen," or "truly, I know."

5.13.3.en: Let us notice together how harsh are the consequences of sin ...

5.13.4.en: 1- Spiritual consequences, for because of it a person becomes a curse instead of a blessing, that is, cursed by God until he repents.

5.13.5.en: 2- Social and moral consequences, for he becomes an example and a reproach by whom people swear: "[the quotation is garbled in the source and cannot be translated]"

5.13.6.en: 3- Bodily consequences, in that the body is struck by illnesses that weary it as a direct result of this sin.

5.13.7.en: So take heed, my brother, and do not make light of sin, for it is exceedingly sinful and calls for repentance and confession so that you may obtain the mercies of God.

5.14.0.en: The priest writes what he said orally to the woman on a piece of skin or a wooden tablet, and he may also write the woman's name with the curses, and puts what he wrote into the water in the earthen vessel, and the writing is blotted out. The meaning intended here is that the water the woman will drink has become the bearer of the curse that the priest pronounced, so that when the woman drinks of this water it enters her inwards to cause her the bitter consequences of sin if she has in fact sinned.

5.15.0.en: It is understood from these two verses that before the woman drank of the water, the priest would take a handful of the offering of ground barley and present it on the outer, ever-burning altar of burnt offering to burn it before the Lord, as was the custom with the other offerings (Lev 2:2), while the rest of the quantity of barley was the portion of the priest and his house; and when the priest had completed that, the woman drank of the water.

5.16.0.en: If the woman has committed adultery, then when she drinks the water her belly swells and her thigh falls away.

5.17.0.en: But if the woman is innocent, the result is God's declaration of her innocence, so no sign of sickness appears on her; on the contrary, as Jewish tradition says, she would increase in beauty, and her life would be blessed, and God would lift up her head before her people, and her pregnancy would be completed to its end, and she would rejoice in her child.

5.17.1.en: The teachers of the Jews say that if the man had fallen into adultery and accused his wife of adultery, and she was in fact an adulteress and drank of the water of the curse, no symptoms appeared on her because of her husband's adultery. For this reason, when corruption and adultery spread among the children of Israel, they neglected to carry out this law, as in the days of Hosea the prophet (Hos 4:13, 14).

5.18.0.en: These two verses are a summary of all that came in the law of jealousy, with which Moses ends his discourse about its procedures, steps and results.

5.19.0.en: When this law is completed the husband is cleared of guilt, even if his wife is innocent, because he did not hasten to condemn her or kill her or divorce her, but left the whole matter to the judgment of God.

5.19.1.en: As for the woman, she bears her guilt if she is at fault and is exposed to God's punishment as He said.

5.19.2.en: Notes on the law of jealousy: from Jewish tradition we can add some matters connected with this law.

5.19.3.en: 1- If the woman confessed before drinking the water, she was divorced from her husband and was given no compensation in anything.

5.19.4.en: 2- If the woman refused to drink, they would force her to.

5.19.5.en: 3- But if she tried to vomit this water, she was driven out and considered unclean.

5.19.6.en: May we all learn not to pass judgment on anyone but to leave matters to God, for He alone is the One who knows and He is also just ... Prayer and committing matters to Him is the best counsel and teaching we can receive from the law of jealousy in this chapter.

5.19.7.en: The law of vows and the priestly blessing, the introduction of the chapter:

5.19.8.en: After God declared His care for His people and they were counted and numbered, and each of them had a name (a standard) by which he was known to God, and a dwelling around His house (the Tent) or a work within it, God brings us through this chapter into a more special relationship, as we shall see.
